expectation: Membrane/cytoplasmic stain of APCs: dendritic, stellate macrophages and DCs scattered densely in gut lamina propria, plus B cells in lymphoid aggregates; small-intestinal epithelium can be MHC-II positive at lower level. Common in mucosa.
notes: Bright branching HLADRA cells fill the lamina propria cores of the villi and overlap CD163 macrophages in row E, with HLADRA-only DC-like cells as well. The epithelium has a dimmer haze, which fits epithelial MHC-II in the gut.
observed: A: bright yellow cores run up the villi and crypts in the mucosa. B: bright stellate cells in the lamina propria; the epithelium is more diffusely lit. C: dimmer epithelium with one bright cell. D: one dendritic-shaped cell. E: branched HLADRA cells, many white on CD163 cells, some green only.
why: Stellate HLADRA+ cells sit in the lamina propria and partly overlap CD163 macrophages, as expected for antigen-presenting cells in the gut.
